approval_note: Implemented under D28 (Phase 4 authorisation, 2026-11-16). Curated by Trace; presented for the owner's review in the Phase 4 report.
curation_note: Templates are instantiated per requirement from the user's own assessment: Gap -> Build (stage 1) and Demonstrate (stage 2); Transferable -> Demonstrate (stage 2) and Reposition (stage 3); Demonstrated -> Reposition (stage 3) only; Unknown -> resolve the missing information first (stage 0), no capability action. Stage 4 is always considered. No courses, providers, costs, timelines, placement outcomes or job openings are named or implied; current openings come only from verified postings in the knowledge base.

where_values.internal_move: Through an internal move or project in your organisation
where_values.external_project: In a self-directed or volunteer project
where_values.self_directed_study: Self-directed study of the cited sources

templates.objective: Understand how product teams learn what users need
templates.action: Study how the cited frameworks describe user-centred insight, then plan five short interviews with users or internal customers of something you work on, with the questions you would ask and what decision each answer could change.
templates.deliverable: A one-page research plan: who you will speak to, your questions, and the decisions they inform

templates.objective: Show that you learn from users and act on it
templates.action: Run the interviews (or analyse existing feedback or support tickets), summarise what users need, and propose one change based on it to the people who decide.
templates.deliverable: An insight summary with the proposed change and what happened to it

templates.objective: Understand how a product direction becomes a sequenced roadmap
templates.action: Study how the cited frameworks describe roadmapping and strategic ownership, then write a short product direction for a product you know: the problem, who it is for, and three outcomes in priority order.
templates.deliverable: A one-page product direction with a sequenced, outcome-based roadmap

templates.objective: Show that you can set and sequence direction for a product area
templates.action: Offer to draft the next-quarter priorities for a feature area or internal tool you work on, explain the order you chose, and get it reviewed by the person who owns the area.
templates.deliverable: A reviewed roadmap for one area, with the reasoning behind its order

templates.objective: Learn to turn a problem into clear requirements and priorities
templates.action: Take a problem you have seen at work and write it up as a problem statement, user stories with acceptance criteria, and a short reason for their order.
templates.deliverable: A written problem statement with prioritised user stories and acceptance criteria

templates.objective: Show that your requirements and priorities are used by a team
templates.action: Write the requirements for one real piece of work your team takes on, agree the priority order with the team, and follow it through to delivery.
templates.deliverable: Requirements a team built from, with the agreed order and the delivered result

templates.objective: Understand how product outcomes are defined and measured
templates.action: Study how the cited frameworks describe managing product outcomes, then pick a feature you know and define its outcome, one success metric, its baseline and how you would read the result.
templates.deliverable: A one-page metric definition: outcome, metric, baseline and decision rule

templates.objective: Show that you own an outcome metric and decide from it
templates.action: Agree a success metric for one feature or process change in your team before it ships, track it afterwards, and write up what it showed and what was decided.
templates.deliverable: A before-and-after metric review with the decision it led to

templates.objective: Understand how product work aligns people with different goals
templates.action: Map the stakeholders of a product or project you know: what each needs, where they disagree, and how a decision between them should be made and communicated.
templates.deliverable: A stakeholder map with a communication plan for one contested decision

templates.objective: Show that you lead cross-functional decisions
templates.action: Facilitate one decision that involves at least two other functions (for example engineering and sales): prepare the options, run the discussion, and circulate the decision and its reasons.
templates.deliverable: A written decision record with the options, the outcome and who agreed

templates.objective: Understand iterative delivery across a product's life cycle
templates.action: Study how the cited sources describe agile and lean practice and life-cycle management, then outline how one feature you know could have shipped in smaller increments, each with something to learn.
templates.deliverable: An increment plan for one feature with what each increment tests

templates.objective: Show that you run iterative delivery
templates.action: Take one piece of work through at least two increments with your team, reviewing what was learned after each before deciding the next.
templates.deliverable: Short review notes for each increment and the change they led to

templates.objective: Build hands-on product analytics skills
templates.action: Using a public or anonymised dataset, write the queries for a funnel and a retention view, and explain what each shows and what you would test next.
templates.deliverable: A short analysis with queries, two charts and the next experiment you would run

templates.objective: Show that you use product data yourself
templates.action: Answer one open product question in your team with your own query or dashboard, and share the result with the people who decide.
templates.deliverable: A query or dashboard in use, with the question it answered

templates.objective: Understand how products are positioned and launched
templates.action: For a product you know, write who it is for, the problem it solves, how it is priced or sold, and how a launch would reach its first users.
templates.deliverable: A one-page positioning and launch plan

templates.objective: Show go-to-market ownership
templates.action: Work with sales or marketing on one launch or adoption push: agree the target users and message, and track adoption afterwards.
templates.deliverable: A launch brief and the adoption result

templates.objective: Build working knowledge of APIs, platforms and data architecture
templates.action: Read the public API documentation of a product you use, and write how a developer would integrate with it, its main limits and one improvement you would prioritise.
templates.deliverable: A short API review with an improvement and the reason for it

templates.objective: Show technical depth in product decisions
templates.action: Contribute to one technical design discussion for your team's product by writing the user and business trade-offs of the options.
templates.deliverable: A trade-off note used in a technical decision

templates.objective: Build domain and regulatory knowledge for your chosen context
templates.action: Identify the regulator and the main rules that apply to products in your chosen domain, and summarise how they constrain one product decision.
templates.deliverable: A one-page domain brief naming the rules and their product impact

templates.objective: Show domain knowledge in real work
templates.action: Work with compliance or legal on one change in a regulated area and record how the requirement shaped it.
templates.deliverable: A change record showing the domain requirement and its effect

templates.objective: Learn to reason about value, business cases and unit economics
templates.action: Build a simple business case for one feature: who pays or saves, the cost to build and run it, and what would need to be true for it to be worth doing.
templates.deliverable: A one-page business case with the assumptions stated

templates.objective: Show that you weigh value against cost in real decisions
templates.action: Prepare the cost and value case for one real decision in your team and present it to the person who approves it.
templates.deliverable: A business case used in a real decision

templates.objective: Build practical understanding of AI-powered features
templates.action: Specify one AI-powered feature: what it should do, how its quality will be evaluated, what it must never do, and how cost and latency limit the choice of model.
templates.deliverable: A feature specification with an evaluation plan and guardrails

templates.objective: Show hands-on AI product work
templates.action: Help define or run the evaluation of one AI or machine-learning feature in your organisation, or build a small prototype in a project, and record the results.
templates.deliverable: An evaluation record or prototype with its measured results

templates.objective: Understand data quality and governance
templates.action: For one dataset you know, write its key definitions, the quality checks it needs, who may access it and why.
templates.deliverable: A short data contract: definitions, checks and access rules

templates.objective: Show that you improve data quality or governance
templates.action: Introduce one shared definition, quality check or access rule for data your team relies on, and get it adopted.
templates.deliverable: An adopted definition, check or rule, with where it is used

templates.objective: Understand portfolio-level product decisions
templates.action: Compare two products or initiatives you know: their goals, shared dependencies and how you would divide investment between them.
templates.deliverable: A short portfolio note with a recommended split and its reasoning

templates.objective: Show scope across several products or a complex, high-risk product
templates.action: Take on a second product area or initiative, or the riskiest part of your current one, and own its decisions alongside your existing work.
templates.deliverable: Decisions you owned across more than one area, with their results

templates.objective: Prepare to coach and mentor others
templates.action: Write how you would onboard a new team member to your area: what they need to learn, in which order, and how you would check progress.
templates.deliverable: An onboarding and coaching plan for one person

templates.objective: Show coaching and product leadership
templates.action: Mentor a junior colleague on a real piece of product work, with regular check-ins and feedback.
templates.deliverable: A mentoring record and the colleague's outcome

templates.objective: Learn to communicate decisions to senior leaders
templates.action: Write a one-page decision paper for a senior audience on a decision you know: the situation, the options, your recommendation and the risks.
templates.deliverable: A one-page decision paper

templates.objective: Show executive-level communication
templates.action: Present progress, risks or a decision for your area to a senior leader or leadership meeting, and record what was decided.
templates.deliverable: The paper or slides used and the decision recorded

templates.objective: Understand planning across teams
templates.action: Map the dependencies between teams for one initiative you know and propose an order of work that removes the biggest blocker first.
templates.deliverable: A cross-team dependency map with a proposed sequence

templates.objective: Show planning across teams and functions
templates.action: Coordinate one initiative that needs at least two teams: agree the dependencies and sequence with both, and track it to completion.
templates.deliverable: A shared cross-team plan and its delivery record

templates.objective: Present existing evidence as product evidence
templates.action: Rewrite the line "{record_excerpt}" for applications so it states what you owned, the decision you made and the result, in the language of "{requirement_title}".
templates.deliverable: A rewritten resume line and a short interview story for this requirement

templates.objective: Explain how related experience carries over
templates.action: Rewrite the line "{record_excerpt}" to show how it carries over to "{requirement_title}", and once you have done the stage 2 action, add that result next to it.
templates.deliverable: A rewritten resume line that links your experience to this requirement

templates.objective: Confirm your draft records
templates.action: Review the draft records Trace lists here and confirm, correct or reject each one.
templates.deliverable: Every listed draft confirmed, corrected or rejected

templates.objective: Categorise your experience
templates.action: Categorise the listed lines of experience by area of responsibility, or mark them "None of these areas".
templates.deliverable: Every listed line categorised

templates.objective: Check older categories against the new areas
templates.action: Open the listed lines and check whether any of the newer areas fit; save them again even if nothing changes.
templates.deliverable: Every listed line checked against the current list of areas

templates.objective: Answer the scope questions
templates.action: Answer the yes/no scope question on the listed lines (choose "Not sure" only if you really are).
templates.deliverable: The scope question answered on every listed line

templates.objective: Add your experience
templates.action: Add your jobs and what you did in them, then confirm them, so Trace can compare your experience with the target role.
templates.deliverable: At least one confirmed job with its responsibilities

templates.objective: Add evidence Trace cannot infer
templates.action: If you have experience of "{requirement_title}", add it to your profile as a responsibility or skill; Trace never assumes it is missing.
templates.deliverable: Any relevant experience added and confirmed

templates.objective: Apply where the stated criteria fit
templates.action: Review the verified current postings listed with this plan, starting with those whose stated criteria you meet; check each on the employer's own site before applying.
templates.deliverable: Applications to postings whose stated criteria you meet, each checked on the employer's site

templates.objective: Find current openings yourself
templates.action: Trace has no verified current posting for this role that you can be matched against. Search employers' own career pages and compare each posting's stated criteria with your confirmed experience.
templates.deliverable: A list of openings you found, each with its stated criteria and the date you checked it

templates.objective: Position your application for the role
templates.action: Lead your resume and application with the requirements you have demonstrated, then the ones that carry over, using the lines rewritten in stage 3.
templates.deliverable: A tailored resume and a short summary statement for this role

templates.objective: Learn from people already in the role
templates.action: Ask people you already work with or know in this role how they got in and how their teams hire; ask for a referral only where they know your work.
templates.deliverable: Notes from your conversations, and any referrals offered

templates.objective: Prepare for interviews on your weaker areas
templates.action: Prepare one specific example for each requirement listed here, using your stage 2 results where you have them, and practise explaining what you would do differently.
templates.deliverable: One prepared example per listed requirement

templates.objective: Consider an internal route
templates.action: Ask your manager or the product team in your organisation whether product roles or product projects are open to internal candidates, and what they would want to see from you.
templates.deliverable: A conversation with the people who decide, and what they said

templates.objective: Move into the bridge role first
templates.action: Look for {bridge_title} roles whose responsibilities match those listed with this route, check their stated entry criteria, and apply where they fit; plan the move to {target_title} from there.
templates.deliverable: Applications to {bridge_title} roles whose responsibilities develop your gaps
